opening_message:
Ticket 1: Diana Cooper (employee ID E020) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E020.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Diana Cooper (E020) is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is permitted under policy. Requested admin; recommend admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E020 is a contractor with basic security training (note in memory saying full_time appears inaccurate). Contractors max is read without advanced training; admin is never permitted. Requested admin, so grant max of read.
reason: The Security agent's note, based on a lookup in its own database, states E020 is a contractor with basic security training and explicitly flags the full_time note as inaccurate. Under policy, contractors may have at most read access without advanced security training, and admin is never permitted for contractors. The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (read), so I grant the maximum of read.
